_readme: Canine dermatology MEDICINES — 15 European markets. An ESTIMATE built from public sources.
No source measures this market in any country; every monetary figure is MODELLED.
Reproducible source for derm-europe.html. Cut-off 6 Aug 2026.
The panel is NOT a European total — it covers 74.1M of Europe's ~106M dogs (about 70%).

method.formula: per country: dogs x {8%,12%,18%} treated x medicine cost per treated dog
method.medicine_cost: EUR 61.6 (Poland, 265 zl / 4.30) x country price level / 72; low and high scaled by 145/265 and 385/265
method.rule: Clinical rates transfer between countries; prices do not. The 8-18% rate is identical everywhere; cost varies by country.

assumptions.name: treated share
assumptions.source: UK VetCompass, skin disorders 12.58% of dogs in one year
assumptions.strength: WEAK outside the UK - no other country publishes an equivalent

assumptions.name: medicine cost
assumptions.value: 265 zl (~EUR 62) per treated dog in Poland, range 145-385
assumptions.strength: WEAK - no source publishes an average; blended from episode and chronic case

assumptions.name: chronic share
assumptions.strength: THE MOST INFLUENTIAL INPUT - at 5% panel falls ~a third, at 20% rises ~a half

assumptions.name: price scaling
assumptions.value: Eurostat comparative price levels, household consumption 2024, EU27=100
assumptions.strength: Likely OVERSTATES the spread - medicines are traded goods with narrower price dispersion than general consumption

totals.sensitivity_dampened_price_scaling: EUR 649M central if the price-level dispersion is halved - the more likely figure of the two
totals.top_5_markets: UK, Germany, Italy, Spain, France = ~EUR 540M = 72% of the panel

external_check.gap: 1.4-1.6x with overlapping ranges - reasonable agreement for a market nobody measures

vendor_country_data_fails_its_own_test.verdict: The vendor's Germany figure carries 2.0x what its dog population and prices justify.
vendor_country_data_fails_its_own_test.second_test: It implies EUR 240-283 of medicine per treated German dog, requiring EUR 150-211 of medicine for a simple episode. Retail prices contradict this.

limitations: Romania counts pet dogs only; 0.6-1.0M street dogs excluded as they generate no medicine sales.
Price levels confirmed for DK 143, BE 117, DE 109, IT 98, ES 91, CZ 88, GR 86, HU 74, PL 72, RO 64. Approximate for UK ~117, FR ~109, SE ~119, AT ~120, PT ~88.
Not in panel: Netherlands, Ireland, Finland, Bulgaria, Croatia, Slovakia, Baltics, Norway, Switzerland, non-EU Europe.
EU veterinary prices up ~37% since 2015 and running ~6%/yr vs ~2% general inflation; older inputs understate current spend.
No deflator applied; single recent year (2022-2026), not a time series.
Country estimates are LESS reliable than the panel total - errors cancel in aggregate and compound individually.

sources.what: Facts & Figures, dog populations by country (2022-23)
Prevalence of disorders in UK dogs under primary veterinary care
Comparative price levels, household final consumption, 2024
Europe and Germany veterinary dermatology drugs — comparison only, not used

trend._honesty: The market itself has never been measured over time, so it has no observable history. What follows is (a) the measured history of its drivers, (b) the one audited series close to the market, and (c) a MODELLED decade backcast.
trend.structural_break: The market in its current shape dates from 2014. Before oclacitinib (Apoquel, 2014) and lokivetmab (Cytopoint, 2017), chronic canine skin disease was managed with corticosteroids costing cents a day plus a small cyclosporine niche. A trend drawn through earlier years on today's definition would be meaningless.

zoetis_dermatology_revenue_usd_million.source: Zoetis SEC filings and earnings releases; global, all species, Apoquel + Cytopoint
zoetis_dermatology_revenue_usd_million.caveat: One company's revenue, not the market — but these products dominate the premium segment.

dogs_europe.2023: ~104-106M — BREAK: largely a FEDIAF survey-coverage change, not real one-year growth; not treated as growth.

trend.prices: EU veterinary prices +~37% since 2015, still ~6%/yr vs ~2% general inflation.

decomposition.therapy_shift: x2.0 (chronic segment ~2% on steroids -> 10% on modern therapies)

modelled_backcast.consistency_check: Modelled 14%/yr market growth vs measured 18%/yr franchise growth — consistent, as the franchise also took share from steroids.

forward_view.if_drivers_persist: ~8-10%/yr; doubling in 7-9 years. The therapy-shift engine is largely spent in Western Europe but not in CEE.
forward_view.what_would_break_it: Loss of exclusivity on the two dominant molecules — generic JAK inhibitors would grow treated volume but shrink value.
